steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine sugar, persimmon pulp, eggs, and baking soda in a mixing bowl. Mix well.
Add flour, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and salt. Pour in milk and melted butter. Stir to combine.
Pour into the baking pan and bake in the preheated oven for 55 minutes. The pudding will rise but will fall when removed from the oven.
Serve with whipped cream or caramel sauce, if desired. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Persimmon Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This persimmon pudding is made with persimmon pulp, spices, eggs, sugar, flour, and butter and baked for a delectable cake-like dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Persimmon Pudding

recipeInstructions.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine sugar, persimmon pulp, eggs, and baking soda in a mixing bowl. Mix well.
Add flour, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and salt. Pour in milk and melted butter. Stir to combine.
Pour into the baking pan and bake in the preheated oven for 55 minutes. The pudding will rise but will fall when removed from the oven.
Serve with whipped cream or caramel sauce, if desired. Enjoy!

review.reviewBody: This is the same recipe that has been in our family for 130 years -- with just one change. If you stir the pudding every 15 minutes while baking, you won't get a crusty top, and it will be less cake-like and more like a true pudding. Very rich, so we just top with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream. Its also delicious cold.

This is an unusual dessert--people look at it with doubt in their eyes, but once they taste it they are converted. Of course, the butter sauce (follows) is a key part--cut the pudding into squares, place on individual serving plates with an ample drizzle of butter sauce. Two cups of persimmon pulp equals 5-6 persimmons, peeled and blended in a food processor. I eliminated the baking powder because we like a dense pudding, and the little bit of soda works just fine. If you do that, you must use buttermilk rather than plain milk. I cut the sugar back to 1-1/2 cups and upped the vanilla to 1 tsp. The baking time required for me was 1 hour and 10 minutes. This also freezes well, wrapped tightly in foil. Make it in season, enjoy all year. Butter sauce: Combine in saucepan: 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup sugar, 1/2 cup cream, pinch of salt and 1-1/2 tsp. vanilla. Heat until sugar is melted and mixture is smooth.

I cut the sugar by 1/2 c. Stir twice in 15 minute intervals. I might add a dash of nutmeg next time. This is great with ice cream or whipped cream.
Additional note: I have made this 3 times now and it is important to adjust the recipe based on the type of persimmon you are using hachiya (round deep orange) persimmons are very sweet and give this pudding a great caramelized sugar flavor. You can cut another 1/4 cup sugar when using hachiyas. The fuyu persimmons are less sweet. I use 2 cups sugar for them.

Wow! I'm so impressed! This turned out so beautifully. I did not poke it every 15 minutes as I did want a cakey finished product and I finished cooking at 52 minutes and gave it time to cool. I also only made half the recipe and used a 9x5 square pan to accomplish the same size and density as I would've with the larger recipe. I'm rating the recipe 5 star without my adjustments as it got everything right. What I changed for myself was making it a bit more "holiday spiced " by adding 1/8 tsp of each: nutmeg, allspice and powdered ginger and 1 full tsp of each: vanilla and cinnamon. Yum yum yum. Enjoy!

Delicious persimmon flavor and a really interesting texture, a cross between cake and pudding...we did cook it about 15 minutes longer than the recipe called for so it wasn't still like batter in the middle. I agree that it's a bit too sweet and will probably make again some time with a cup less sugar.

Update: Made again with one cup less sugar and half a cup less milk for 60 minutes and it came out just about perfect.

I used 2 cups sugar instead of 2 and 1/2 and it was still plenty sweet. I also added 1/4 tsp cloves and 1/4 tsp nutmeg for just a little more spice. Very good pudding. Although mine was still a bit soft/wet in the middle after 55 mins, so I will cook it 10-15 mins longer next time and keep an eye on it. :)

I noted what the other reviewers said about the recipe being too sweet and reduced the sugar to 1/2 c. To keep the pudding from being too soupy after eliminating so much sugar, I decreased the milk to 2 c. Tasted great!

Delicious but too sweet. I cut the sugar to 1.5 c. Next time I’ll cut the sugar back to 1 c. Also cook time was at least 30 min longer. But it was amazing - very similar to what my mother used to make. A little whipped cream puts it over the top.
I love persimmon pudding but being a diabetic I cannot have the sugar. I replaced the sugar with dates and the flour with almond flour so that the carbs and glycemic index were low too.

Good! I had only 1 persimmon, so I halved the recipe. The fruit was so sweet, and the sugar content scared me a little, so I reduced the sugar to 1 cup and used some sour milk. I also used whole wheat flour for about 1/3 of the flour portion. Still quite sweet, but very nice warm with whipped cream. I'll probably double the cinnamon and add the same amount of cardamom the next time I make this. Will continue to use soured or buttermilk. Then it will likely be 5 stars.

My husband loved the recipe as it reminded him of toffee pudding. The recipe is quick and easy. If you've never had ripe persimmon, it's very sweet on its own. I reduced the sugar to 1 1/2 cups and followed the rest of the recipe as written. It's very good. Just be aware that if you don't like "super sweet" desserts, the recipe as written may be too sweet but you can always scale back the sugar and it's delicious!

This is delicious! We were gifted several persimmon so I searched for what I could make. This persimmon pudding was perfect. I kept it cake-like on purpose (didn’t stir as someone else suggested). I used less sugar (just under 2 cups) and added nutmeg. It’s like a very moist gingerbread and fantastic. Thank you!

Maybe I used the wrong type of flour but the dry to wet ratio of ingredients leaves this way too wet. I ditched the milk and it still took forever to cook and came out fudgey. Way too sweet. Sugar overpowered permission flavour. I think that the wet and dry ingredients should be mixed seperate and the wet added to the dr as to avoid lumps. I would think this was AI if there weren't so many positive reviews.
Been cooking 60 minutes in a 9x13. Still not done SUPER THICK pudding. Its fuller than any cake I've ever made.
Made it exactly as the recipe called for. It was delicious. Added caramel sauce and whipped cream.
I made no changes/modifications to the recipe and absolutely love it, as does my wife.
Easy to make, satisfying to eat. I added 1/4 tsp of nutmeg, and for the second batch I added a handful of currants.
Great recipe, very easy to make. I reduced sugar to 1 cup and milk to 2 cups and increased the persimmon pulp to 2.5 cups. It came out unbelievably good! Thank you for the recipe!
I added 1/4 teaspoon of Nutmeg also

Way too much sugar. I put less than half the amount listed. Also how is this 8 servings? There was enough pudding to feed a large family. Flavour of the persimmons doesn't really translate well in my opinion, but it's nice enough to eat. Wouldn't necessarily repeat.
